standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the morphism g : Y'' -> Y' together with D'' and p : D'' -> D' whose defining property is that a class on D' is determined by its pullback to D'', which is the uniqueness used twice at the end of the proof.

core_obligations: Fix the data to be checked: for a locally of finite type Y' -> Y, a triple (L', s', i' : D' -> Y') as in the Gysin definition with pullback (N', t', j' : E' -> X') to X', one has to show c cap (i')^* alpha' = (j')^*(c cap alpha') for every class alpha' on Y' (proof lines 6537-6543).

Introduce the auxiliary smooth morphism of relative dimension one: denote g : Y'' -> Y' with i'' : D'' -> Y'' and p : D'' -> D' as constructed by the normal cone lemma, warn that D'' is not the full inverse image of D', and denote by f : X'' -> X' and E'' the base changes; from the defining property of this construction the class beta' = (i')^* alpha' is the unique element of CH_{k-1}(D') with p^* beta' = (i'')^* g^* alpha', and gamma' = (j')^*(c cap alpha') is the unique element of CH_{k-1-p}(E') with q^* gamma' = (j'')^* h^*(c cap alpha') (proof lines 6545-6564).

Conclude by the uniqueness: the assumed conditions on c, applied to i'' and its base change j'' whose normal bundles are trivial by construction, give (j'')^* h^*(c cap alpha') = c cap (i'')^* g^* alpha' and q^*(c cap beta') = c cap p^* beta'; combining these with the two uniqueness statements shows gamma' = c cap beta', which is the missing condition (proof lines 6565-6578).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to checking condition (3) for a single triple on Y' (proof lines 6537-6543).
Build the smooth relative dimension one model where the divisor has trivial normal bundle and identify both classes by the resulting uniqueness (proof lines 6545-6564).
Apply the assumed weak form of condition (3) to that model and conclude by uniqueness (proof lines 6565-6578).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a rule assigning pullback maps on Chow groups and satisfying the bivariant conditions (1) and (2) together with condition (3) only for divisors with trivial conormal bundle is already a full bivariant class (statement lines 6518-6535, tag 0F9A). The proof is a genuine reduction: it replaces the given triple by a smooth morphism of relative dimension one built from the normal cone lemma, on which the conormal bundle is trivial by construction, uses the characterising uniqueness of that construction for two different classes, and then transfers the hypothesis along the base change to conclude the missing condition (3). The construction and the two uniqueness comparisons are the substance, so the claim is H2.
